prompt: We're considering switching our 200-person engineering team from Java to Rust at Meridian Financial Systems, a mid-size fintech company processing 2M transactions/day. The CTO believes Rust's memory safety and performance will reduce our production incidents by 60%. Map the cascade effects across all affected domains.
expected_output: A cascade map covering 5+ domains with 1st/2nd/3rd order effects and feedback loops
expectations: Output identifies 5 or more distinct domains affected (e.g., engineering team, hiring/talent, customers, product velocity, vendor/tooling ecosystem, finance/budget)
Output traces at least 2 orders of effects beyond first-order for the majority of domains
Output identifies at least 2 feedback loops with mechanism explanations
Output labels feedback loops as amplifying or dampening
Output is structured with clear domain-by-domain organization
Output includes at least 1 counter-intuitive or non-obvious effect
Output provides mechanisms (why/because) for causal chains, not just listing effects

prompt: My manager at Nexus Analytics wants to mandate daily standup meetings for all 12 remote teams across 4 time zones (US Pacific, US Eastern, London, Bangalore). Currently teams do async updates in Slack. She believes standups will 'increase accountability and team cohesion.' Help me think through the effects.
expected_output: A cascade map covering 5+ domains with 1st/2nd/3rd order effects and feedback loops
expectations: Output identifies 5 or more distinct domains affected (e.g., team productivity, employee wellbeing/morale, cross-timezone collaboration, hiring/retention, meeting culture, management visibility)
Output traces at least 2 orders of effects beyond first-order for the majority of domains
Output identifies at least 2 feedback loops with mechanism explanations
Output labels feedback loops as amplifying or dampening
Output is structured with clear domain-by-domain organization
Output includes at least 1 counter-intuitive or non-obvious effect (e.g., standups reducing rather than increasing accountability)
Output provides mechanisms (why/because) for causal chains, not just listing effects
